title: Cap. X controversy-sum continued: non-elect likewise considered sinners worthy of death, no worse in themselves, yet by freest will not dignified with the special mercy prepared for the elect — then Arminius falls, we obtain the cause
pass_a_gloss: And on the contrary, if those who are called non-elect, passed over or reprobate, were also considered by God as sinners worthy of death, although in themselves no whit worse, yet by the freest will of God by no means dignified with the same special mercy and efficacious calling which prepared for the elect wrought their faith, repentance, and salvation, then Arminius sinks, we obtain the cause.
pass_b_english: And on the other side take the non-elect — those called passed over or reprobate. They too were considered by God as sinners worthy of death. In themselves they were no worse. Yet by God's freest will they were not dignified with that same special mercy and efficacious calling which, prepared for the elect, wrought their faith, repentance, and salvation. Then Arminius sinks, and we obtain the cause.
source_text: Et e contra, si qui non-electi, praeteriti sive reprobati dicuntur, fuerunt etiam a Deo considerati ut peccatores morte digni, etsi in se nihilo deteriores, sed liberrima Dei voluntate minime dignati eadem speciali misericordia et efficaci vocatione quae electis praeparata fidem, resipiscentiam et salutem eorum operata est, tum succumbits Arminius, nos causam obtinemus.
